note: SDK fixtures assert-c1 runs against in CI.
These refs must track the stamps the plugins themselves pin — sdk-map.md's source-commit
line and the clone instructions in each getting-started skill. If a plugin is regenerated
against a newer SDK, update it here in the same commit, or CI keeps checking the old one
and reports green about a surface nobody ships any more.
surface is passed to --surface. Assertions that declare a `surfaces` key run only on the
surfaces they name (today: the pre-4.0.0 set in assertions/15-pre-4.0.0.json). The general
328 are NOT filtered — they run in full against every fixture, and the ~100 that cannot
hold on pre-4.0.0 are pinned per-fixture in expectFailures. Failing loudly against a
recorded baseline is more informative than silently running a smaller suite.

fixtures.name: twilio
note: Pinned to the commit sdk-map.md documents. This ref was `main` until 2026-08-28, when the
SDK repo's main was regenerated with a v4-beta generator (3d2efed, 'Regenerate SDK (v4 beta
codegen)') and this job correctly failed 17 surface assertions nine minutes later — the
drift-detection system firing on a live generator move. A branch is not a pin. When the
twilio plugin is regenerated against the new SDK, update this SHA together with the map.

fixtures.name: maxio
note: The pre-4.0.0 surface — 88 Core/*.cs against 4.0.0's 122. 100 of the general assertions
fail here by construction and are baselined; the pre400.* set is the positive half and is
expected to pass. Before this fixture existed, NOTHING checked maxio-sdk's runtime claims:
the suite ran against two 4.0.0 SDKs only, so no assertion had ever been tried on a second
surface and the C1-vs-C2 split the skills rest on was itself unverified.
mutationTest runs the pre-4.0.0 mutation set (MUTATIONS_PRE_4_0_0), which is selected by
--surface. Every mutation there makes this surface look MORE like 4.0.0 — the realistic
direction of drift, and the one that would silently invalidate maxio-sdk's skills, whose
whole premise is that this surface is not that one. Five of the fourteen pre400.*
assertions are `absent` regexes, and an `absent` regex matching nothing looks exactly like
one that is simply wrong; this is what rules that out.
The generator's own StaticCode/ — the authority on what the NEXT generated plugin gets.
It is expected to fail: it still stamps 4.0.0 while its Core has moved ahead of both SDKs
above. generator-template-drift.txt records exactly which assertions fail, and the job goes
red only when that set CHANGES. A permanently red job teaches people to ignore it.
Private repo, so the job needs a token and skips cleanly without one.
